questions.prompt: During overload resolution, what happens when `std::enable_if_t<false, int>` is formed in a function template's return type?
options: Compilation halts immediately with an error inside namespace std
Substitution fails in the immediate context and that candidate is silently removed from the overload set
The return type defaults to void and the template remains viable
std::enable_if_t throws std::bad_typeid at runtime
questions.explanation: Under [temp.deduct], when `Cond` is false, `std::enable_if<false, int>` has no member `type`. Because this failure occurs in the immediate context of the function template's return type, SFINAE removes the candidate silently.

questions.prompt: How do `template <class T> void f(T x) requires std::integral<T>;` and `void f(std::integral auto x);` compare in C++20?
options: Both declare function templates constrained by std::integral on the deduced parameter type
Only the abbreviated form works with concepts; trailing requires only checks runtime values
Abbreviated auto allows virtual member functions whereas trailing requires forbids them
Abbreviated auto performs type erasure like std::any instead of template instantiation
questions.explanation: Under [dcl.fct] and [temp.constr.decl], an abbreviated function template using a type-constraint before `auto` introduces an invented constrained template type parameter with the same constraint semantics.

questions.prompt: What does `AlwaysTrue<double>` evaluate to in the concept definition below?
options: false, because double is not the same type as int
Ill-formed: concepts cannot appear inside a requires-expression
false, because std::same_as evaluates at runtime
true, because without a nested `requires`, the line only checks whether the expression `std::same_as<double, int>` compiles
questions.explanation: Inside a requires-expression, `std::same_as<T, int>;` without a leading `requires` is a simple requirement ([expr.prim.req.simple]). Since `std::same_as<double, int>` is a valid bool expression yielding `false`, the simple requirement succeeds and `AlwaysTrue<double>` is `true`!

questions.prompt: Why is calling `pick(42)` ambiguous between these two constrained overloads?
options: sizeof(T) >= 2 is not a constant expression when T is deduced
The two inline `sizeof(T) >= 2` expressions are separate atomic constraints with distinct source identities, so neither subsumes the other
Subsumption only applies to class templates, never function templates
std::integral<T> cannot be combined with && inside a requires clause
questions.explanation: Under [temp.constr.atomic] and [temp.constr.order], subsumption compares normalized atomic constraints by declaration identity and parameter mapping—not mathematical equivalence. Only factoring `sizeof(T) >= 2` into a shared named concept enables subsumption.

questions.prompt: Which failure triggers a hard compilation error rather than being silently discarded by SFINAE when instantiating for `T = int`?
options: Forming `typename T::value_type` directly in a function template's return type
Forming an invalid call `decltype(std::declval<T&>().push_back(0))` in a trailing return type
A static_assert or invalid typedef triggered inside a helper struct's class definition instantiated during substitution
Failing a concept check in a function template's trailing requires-clause
questions.explanation: Under [temp.deduct], SFINAE covers only errors in the immediate context of the function type and template parameter expressions. Instantiating a separate class template body to inspect its members leaves the immediate context and causes a hard error.
